ideas_and_plots.title: Mystery Story Ideas & Plot Outlines
ideas_and_plots.intro: A mystery works when the reader can follow the detective's reasoning and still be surprised by the final solution. Start with a crime, a closed circle of suspects, and one clue that only makes sense at the end.
ideas_and_plots.twist_title: Mystery story ideas with a twist
ideas_and_plots.twist_intro: These premises give the generator a reveal that changes the meaning of the clues rather than cancelling them.

items.title: The witness who was never there
items.description: Every suspect describes the same witness, but the witness died before the crime.

items.title: The alibi that proves guilt
items.description: The suspect's perfect alibi is the clue that places them at the scene.

items.title: The victim's own plan
items.description: The murder was staged by the victim to expose someone else, and the detective has to solve a crime that has not happened yet.

items.title: The confession in the wrong voice
items.description: A recorded confession is real, but the person speaking it was not the killer.

murder_mystery.title: Murder Mystery Generator
murder_mystery.intro: Use the murder subgenre when you want a clear crime, a set of suspects, and a solution that can be proved. The generator produces a body, a closed circle, and a clue trail rather than a generic thriller chase.
paragraphs: The murderer should be present in the story before the reveal, and the decisive clue should be available to the reader. The generator is instructed to plant evidence, distinguish red herrings from proof, and make the final solution follow from the clues.
Choose the short length for a complete case, or the full plot outline when you need acts, suspects, and a reveal to revise.

how_to.title: How to Build a Mystery Plot Step by Step
how_to.intro: A mystery plot is a chain of cause and effect. Build it in four moves so the reader can follow the logic and still feel the surprise.

steps.title: Crime
steps.description: Establish what happened, who was harmed, and why the detective cannot walk away.

steps.title: Clues
steps.description: Plant physical and testimonial evidence early. Each clue should eliminate one explanation and open another.

steps.title: Suspects
steps.description: Give every suspect a motive, an opportunity, and a lie that makes sense to them.

steps.title: Reveal
steps.description: Show how the solution follows from the clues. The final answer should feel inevitable in retrospect, not arbitrary.

clues.title: Clues, Red Herrings and the Twist
clues.intro: A fair mystery distinguishes three things: evidence that proves something, evidence that misleads without cheating, and a twist that changes the meaning of both.

items.title: Fair clue
items.description: A detail the reader can see and interpret before the detective explains it.

items.title: Red herring
items.description: A plausible lead that points to a real secret, just not the one the reader assumed.

items.title: Twist
items.description: A reveal that re-reads the established evidence instead of introducing a new fact at the last moment.

comparison.title: Mystery vs Thriller: Which Generator Do You Need?
comparison.intro: Mystery and thriller overlap, but they promise different reading experiences. Choose mystery when the question is 'who did it and how can we prove it?'
comparison.mystery: Mystery focuses on the puzzle: clues, suspects, deduction, and a solution the reader can verify.
comparison.thriller: Thriller focuses on danger and urgency: the protagonist is trying to prevent the next harm rather than explain the last one.

definition.title: What is a Mystery Story Generator?
definition.intro: A mystery story generator turns a premise into a case: a crime, a set of suspects, a clue trail, and a solution. It is a drafting tool for structure, not a substitute for your own judgement.
paragraphs: The useful output is the chain of evidence. A good mystery gives the reader enough information to suspect the truth before the detective explains it, while keeping the final confirmation satisfying.

Use the generated draft to test whether the clues are fair. Replace generic details with your own setting, check that every suspect had a real opportunity, and make sure the reveal does not depend on information the reader never had.

faq_section.label: FAQ
faq_section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_section.description: Common questions about the mystery story generator, its subgenres, and how to use the output.

items.title: Is there a free mystery story generator?
items.description: Yes. This page is free to start, with no sign-up required for the first generation. You can generate a hook, a short story, or a full plot outline.

items.title: Can AI write a good mystery story?
items.description: It can produce a usable draft, especially when you give it a specific case and a fair clue trail. A good mystery still depends on your judgement: check the logic, replace generic details, and make sure the reveal follows from the evidence.

items.title: How do I come up with a mystery plot?
items.description: Start with a crime, a closed circle of suspects, and one contradiction. Then decide what the detective can prove, what the reader can suspect, and what the final clue changes. The four-step section above turns that into a plot.

items.title: Can I generate a fantasy mystery story?
items.description: Yes. Describe the fantasy setting and the rule that makes the case possible, then choose the mystery subgenre. The generator can keep the clue logic while adding magic, politics, or a invented world.

items.title: Can I generate a romance mystery story?
items.description: Yes. Give the generator a relationship at the centre of the case and decide whether the romance helps or complicates the investigation. The mystery controls still apply.

items.title: What's the difference between a mystery and a thriller?
items.description: A mystery asks who did it and how it can be proved. A thriller asks whether the protagonist can stop the next harm. Mystery is a puzzle; thriller is a pressure sequence.

items.title: Can I generate a crime story instead?
items.description: This page is focused on mystery structure. You can choose the murder subgenre for a crime-driven case, but the output is still built around clues, suspects, and a solution rather than a thriller chase.
